annotations.text:
Live — click the glyph.

It cycles Auto → Light → Dark → Auto, sitting left of Settings in the same 8px-radius, 1px-border, 13px-accent shell as .gearlink.

Auto is the starting state, so the half-moon is what you see in the header by default.

Use the "What the OS says" tweak above this board to check that Auto resolves correctly both ways.

Why one shape and not three icons

A sun/moon pair has no natural third state, and bolting a monitor glyph on for Auto gives you three unrelated shapes in a 16px box.

Fill level has a third state for free: empty → half → full. Auto sits between the two it chooses from, which is what it does.

To build this for real, three things change in server/dashboard.mjs:

1. The light tokens in the prefers-color-scheme block become the Paper values, and both sets move onto a [data-theme] attribute on <html> so an explicit choice can win.
2. Keep the media query as the Auto branch — :root:not([data-theme]) — so Auto is genuinely the OS, not a guess made at load.
3. Persist the choice per browser (localStorage) and set the attribute before first paint, or the page flashes the wrong scheme on every load.
